beats.hook: She grabbed the birthday cake out of my seven-year-old's hands and announced it was her son's turn — at my daughter's birthday party.
beats.normal_life: Mia's party was going perfectly. Twelve kids, a bouncy castle, and a custom unicorn cake I had spent three hours making from scratch — the one detail that mattered more than I knew.
beats.first_red_flag: A woman named Karen — I wish I was making that up — had been hovering near the cake table for twenty minutes. She kept mentioning, loudly, that her son Brody "really loves unicorns too."
beats.the_reveal: The moment I handed Mia the cake for the candles, Karen physically stepped in, took it, and set it in front of Brody. She said, and I quote — "He never gets to be special."
beats.aftermath: The entire yard went silent. Every parent froze. I walked over, picked the cake back up, and placed it in front of my daughter. Then I looked at Karen and said, calmly, "This is her party. You're going to want to step back." She left ten minutes later. Brody cried. Honestly — so did I, once everyone was gone.
beats.cta: What would you have done in that moment — because I still wonder if I handled it right.
